title: Slab allocator + hybrid prefetch & eviction RFC (paged KV)
content:
Summary:

This note sketches a slab-based GPU memory allocator that couples cooperative warp-level prefetching with a hybrid eviction strategy for paged KV caches. The goal is to reduce stalls in FlashAttention-style fused kernels when the paged KV hit rate is low, while keeping allocator fragmentation and peak-device-memory use bounded. This is exploratory: focused on implementation sketch, scheduling heuristics, and microbench experiments.

Motivation / Observed pain points:
- Large models with long-context workloads produce heavy KV churn. Current paged-KV eviction/assignments cause tail latency spikes when kernels miss and block on fetching pages.
- FlashAttention fused kernels are sensitive to sudden increases in latency from H2D transfer or cache thrashing; even short stalls amplify across many tokens due to synchronous token generation.
- Existing per-page allocators lead to fragmentation and uneven reuse; naive background eviction either evicts too aggressively (hurting reuse) or too lazily (hitting OOM).

High-level idea:
- Allocate KV memory in slabs (contiguous device allocations sized to power-of-two multiples of page-size). Slabs are managed by a lightweight slab-allocator with per-slab metadata (free list, refcount epoch, resident-set score).
- Introduce a hybrid prefetch policy that performs cooperative warp-level prefetch packets (using cp.async or async copies where available) into a short-lived prefetch slab before fused kernels start. Prefetch is guided by a per-request predicted access window (based on recent token patterns and model attention locality).
- Eviction is hybrid: LRU-like within a slab (recently used pages are retained), but a probabilistic global sampler chooses slab candidates for proactive eviction to control fragmentation and global memory pressure.
- Add a background eviction worker that runs off-kernel on a separate stream and respects a backpressure budget exposed to schedulers.

Allocator layout and metadata:
- Slab: contiguous device allocation, size = K * page_size (K tuned; default 16 pages ~ 16 * 256KB).
- Per-slab metadata (packed in pinned host mem, small footprint): slab_id, base_ptr (device), capacity_pages, used_pages, last_touch_epoch, hot_score (float), owner_shard_id.
- Page descriptor (compact): page_offset, resident_flag, refcount, last_access_token (epoch id). Store per-slab bitmaps for quick tests.

Prefetch policy (cooperative):
- When a request is scheduled, the scheduler queries the KV predictor for a prefetch window (N pages ahead). The predictor is simple: last-seen attention offsets + positional deltas aggregated over the shard.
- If the target pages are not resident, enqueue a prefetch task on the request stream: perform async memcpy (host pinned staging -> device slab region) or use cudaMemcpyAsync + cp.async intra-kernel when supported. We batch prefetches per warp to amortize H2D latency and align to 128B/256B boundaries.
- Prefetch slab is a small per-shard LRU: pages prefetched here are promoted to long-lived slabs if reused within M tokens. Otherwise they are demoted/evicted quickly.

Eviction strategy (hybrid sampler + LRU):
- Primary eviction: within-slab LRU for fine-grained reuse tuning; maintain per-slab ring buffer of recent page ids (approximate LRU to limit overhead).
- Global sampler: periodically sample S slabs and compute eviction score = hot_score - alpha * fragmentation_penalty. Select candidate slabs with lowest score for batch reclaim.
- Eviction move semantics: evicting a hot page triggers an asynchronous writeback to host staging (if dirty) or immediate device-free if clean. Eviction worker batches writes to maximize PCIe/NVLink efficiency.

Integration with FlashAttention / fused kernels:
- Kernels query the KV handle to pin pages for the token generation window. Pinned pages increase slab refcount and temporarily prevent eviction.
- Introduce a short-lived kernel-visible fence around prefetch completion: fused kernel may issue a lightweight spin/timeout waiting for prefetch on a per-warp basis. Prefer cooperative wake (CUDA events + stream callbacks) to blocking spin.
- When fused ops are using shared memory heavily, scheduler must be aware of extra shared-memory usage for prefetch staging (we may stage small fragments in shared memory for very low-latency pages).

Optimizations and implementation notes:
- Use bitset scan (popcount + trailing-zero) for fast page allocation within slab. Keep per-slab freelist cached in registers/shared memory for hot threads.
- Use 128B-aligned pages for best coalescing with warp accesses; make slab sizes multiples of 64KB to match large page TLB boundaries on Hopper/Ampere where possible.
- Use cp.async + __pipeline for intra-kernel prefetch when kernel structure supports it (saves kernel launch latency). Fall back to async memcpy for older toolchains.
- Keep slab metadata in pinned host memory for lower latency updates from CPU-side eviction worker; but expose a GPU-read-only snapshot for kernels to consult without PCIe roundtrips.
- Quant-aware prefetch: when model uses quantized KV (int8/4-bit), prefetch width increases but staging size decreases; predictor should compensate by expanding window count but respecting bandwidth budget.

Scheduler interaction and backpressure:
- Introduce a PrefetchBudget token per request queue. Each prefetch consumes tokens proportional to bytes requested. PrefetchBudget is periodically refilled by global policy tuned to keep <X% of PCIe bandwidth for prefetching.
- If budget is exhausted, scheduler triggers a lightweight fallback: either accept synchronous miss (slower) or route to a nearby replica with higher residency (if available).
- Expose metrics: prefetch_hit_rate, prefetch_bandwidth_util, avg_prefetch_latency, slab_fragmentation_ratio, eviction_throughput, background_eviction_latency.

Microbench plan (must run before merging):
1) Baseline: current paged-KV with per-page allocator + simple eviction; measure steady-state throughput and 99th token latency for sample workloads (long-context RLHF, multi-document retrievals).
2) Slab allocator only (no prefetch): measure fragmentation, throughput, memory utilization.
3) Add cooperative prefetch (async memcpy): measure improvement in 50/95/99 latencies and bandwidth usage.
4) Add intra-kernel cp.async variant. Compare kernel-level pipe vs memcpy + stream callbacks.
5) Stress tests: adversarial access (randomized page accesses) to measure worst-case eviction/backpressure behavior.
6) Quantized model runs: measure impact on prefetch window and effective bandwidth.

Success criteria:
- 95th token latency reduced by >= 15% on long-context generation benchmarks vs baseline, and 99th token latency reduced by >= 10%.
- No increase in average device memory footprint > 8% (slab overhead allowed but bounded).
- Prefetch hit rate >= 75% under realistic workloads and with budget tuned.

Open questions / risks:
- Predictor accuracy: a weak predictor causes wasted bandwidth and increased eviction churn. Need lightweight adaptive predictor with quick cold-start behaviour.
- Fragmentation: slab sizes mischosen for heterogeneous page sizes can increase internal fragmentation. Mitigate with multiple slab classes (small/medium/large).
- Kernel complexity: moving cp.async intrakernel increases code complexity and register/shared-memory pressure; must validate occupancy tradeoffs on target SMs.
- PCIe vs NVLink heterogeneity: eviction and prefetch heuristics need auto-detect/auto-tune for interconnect topology.

Implementation TODOs (short):
- [ ] Prototype slab allocator + metadata on CPU side (C++), unit tests for correctness.
- [ ] Implement per-slab LRU ring and bitmap allocation helpers.
- [ ] Add async prefetch path using cudaMemcpyAsync + stream callbacks.
- [ ] Build predictor: start with heuristic (recent offsets) + exponential decay counters.
- [ ] Instrument metrics and expose to Console for initial runs.
- [ ] Benchmark harness jobs and adversarial stress generator.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intended as a practical, incremental design that can be landed in stages. Early wins are slab allocator + async memcpy prefetch; cp.async and intra-kernel staging are second-phase optimizations dependent on toolchain and register budget.
- Feedback especially sought on slab sizing defaults, prefetch budget refill heuristics, and whether adding a dirty-writeback path is necessary for our use-cases (we currently expect KV pages to be read-mostly).

Appendix: quick pseudo-code (allocator + prefetch enqueue)

allocate_page(slab_class):
  for slab in class_free_list:
    word = atomic_find_and_reserve_bit(slab.bitmap)
    if word != FAIL:
      slab.used_pages++
      return slab.base_ptr + page_offset(word)
  // fallback: try commit new slab from device allocator
  return commit_new_slab(slab_class)
enqueue_prefetch(request, pages):
  budget = prefetch_budget_acquire(bytes(pages))
  if not budget:
    return PREFETCH_DENIED
  // batch pages by slab
  for slab, page_group in group_by_slab(pages):
    dst = allocate_prefetch_slot(slab)
    cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, host_staging(page_group), size, request.stream)
  // schedule completion event
  cudaEventRecord(prefetch_done, request.stream)
  return PREFETCH_ENQUEUED

End of doc.
